page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6149 processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.hfg5.large delivers entry-level performance across most workloads. In CPU-intensive tests, the instance scored 1346.89 in stress-ng single-core and 1789.49 in multi-core. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read and write speeds measuring under 10 GB/sec. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance is a notable exception, achieving an average score of 8.86 GB/sec.

Due to its dedicated CPU allocation, the instance avoids the CPU credit limitations of burstable types, but its overall compute and memory throughput remain in the lower percentiles. It is not suited for demanding database operations, software compilation, or large language model inference. The instance is best utilized for lightweight general-purpose tasks, basic text processing, single-threaded utilities, or low-traffic static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.large is an entry-level, general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated Intel Xeon 6149 CPU cores running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM and a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks position the instance in the lower percentiles for most compute and memory-bound tasks, with stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores falling in the bottom 10%. However, it maintains average performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Given these performance characteristics and its dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.hfg5.large is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic text processing, simple single-threaded applications, and low-traffic static web serving, offering a predictable but modest resource profile.
